messages:
Alex (Support): Hey team — escalating a customer ticket (TKT-8342). They report intermittent SSE disconnects during long streaming responses: client sees partial output then connection closes. Customer attached a pcap and server logs. They also noticed a transient 429-like billing rejection just before some closes. Repro steps provided by customer below. Ticket: https://redwood/support/tickets/8342

Jordan (Customer): Confirming — when we ask for ~10k token streams (policy evals) the stream often ends mid-chunk. We see socket RST from client side and a 401/403 once in a while, but most closes show TCP FIN from our side. Attaching pcap: https://files.example/pcap/pcap-8342.pcapng. We also captured browser console: 
```
EventSource error: connection closed
status: 200, decoded tokens so far: ~3.2k
reconnect attempts: client retries 3x then gives up
```

Sam (Eng): Thanks. A few quick hypotheses: token expiration/rotate causing auth failures, edge proxy idle/timeout closing connections, or billing quota enforcement kicking and tearing streams. Can you paste the exact Authorization header pattern you use (no token value)? Also which SDK?

Jordan (Customer): Using custom EventSource in React + a short-lived API key we rotate every 15m. Header: `Authorization: Bearer <short-lived>` (we refresh via our backend). SDK is a thin wrapper over fetch/eventsource polyfill.

Mira (SRE): Uploads look good. From the server side I see many streams that end with this pattern in the proxy logs: 
```
[edge-proxy] 2026-11-12T18:14:05Z stream-id=xyz client_ip=1.2.3.4 upstream=200 keepalive=idle_timeout
[edge-proxy] 2026-11-12T18:14:05Z stream-id=xyz teardown: reason=idle_timeout
```
But for a subset there is: 
```
[auth] 2026-11-12T18:14:04Z token=abc status=403 reason=billing_blocked
[edge-proxy] 2026-11-12T18:14:04Z stream-id=abc upstream=499
```
So two classes: 1) idle timeout (we may have a keepalive mismatch), 2) an auth/billing enforcement event that returns 403/499 and triggers stream termination.

Alex (Support): Jordan — can you check whether your backend refresh path attempts a new EventSource open while an old one is still active? We're seeing client-side retried opens that race with token rotate. If the old stream is torn down server-side due to billing/auth check, the client might see a partial stream.

Jordan (Customer): We do attempt to quietly re-open if we detect EventSource closed, but we do not proactively open during refresh. We rotate keys in background using a different call. I can share the client snippet: 
```js
// simplified
const es = new EventSource('/v1/streams?id=abc', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
es.onmessage = (ev) => { renderChunk(ev.data); };
es.onerror = (e) => { console.log('es error', e); };
```

Sam (Eng): Useful. Mira — can you run a quick tcpdump on the ingress node to see if FINs are from the proxy or upstream? Example: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.0.5.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/ingress.pcap` and then `tcpdump -n -r /tmp/ingress.pcap | grep FIN`

Mira (SRE): Did that. Summary: many FINs show as coming from our proxy to client shortly after we log `billing_blocked`. For the idle_timeout cases the FIN aligns with the proxy connection timeout at ~75s. Client heartbeats are at 60s, so slight jitter causes proxy to think connection is idle.

ingest-bot: ALERT: stream.error.rate increased to 4.5% (5m) in region-us-east-1 — rule: stream-errors > 1%

Sam (Eng): Two suggested fixes: 1) short-term: lower proxy idle timeout to 95s or instruct clients to send a lightweight comment/heartbeat every 30s. 2) medium-term: ensure auth/billing check does not eagerly abort active streams but marks them and lets stream finish with 402/metadata footers so consumers get final tokens. We should also add a metric for billing-terminated-streams.

Alex (Support): Jordan — as mitigation can you add a heartbeat `: keepalive \n` every 25s from client? Quick snippet for EventSource polyfill: 
```js
setInterval(() => fetch('/v1/streams/keepalive?id=abc', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } }), 25000);
```
That should prevent idle timeouts.

Jordan (Customer): We'll try that. Question: how were we getting a 403/billing_blocked mid-stream? We had quota but not exhausted.

Mira (SRE): Investigating billing logs. There's an edge-case where a downstream billing reconciliation job marks a usage as suspicious and flips a billing hold for that API key briefly (30-120s) while manual review kicks in. When that happens our auth service returns 403 for new auth checks; because some components revalidate tokens mid-stream (for long streams we re-check every chunk boundary) the auth check fails and the proxy aborts. We should not abort the stream; instead we should let it finish or return a structured error event.

Sam (Eng): Repro steps we used locally to simulate: 1) start a long stream with a test key, 2) trigger billing hold by toggling the key via admin API, 3) observe proxy abort. Commands: 
```
# start a test stream (server side)
python3 tools/run_long_stream.py --tokens 10000 --port 8080
# toggle billing hold
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin" https://api.internal/admin/keys/hold?key=test-123
# monitor logs
tail -f /var/log/edge-proxy.log | grep stream-id
```
We attached a small pcap and logs from our repro: https://artifacts.internal/repro/pcap-hold-1906.pcapng

deploy-bot: deploy redwood/edge-proxy@v2.12.3 completed 2026-11-12T18:10:12Z :rocket:

Mira (SRE): Follow-up actions I'm taking: 
- Add `billing_terminated_streams` counter (Prometheus) and a Grafana panel.
- Tweak auth path to return a stream-safe error (SSE `event: billing_termination\ndata: {"code":"billing_hold"}\n\n`) instead of abruptly closing upstream.
- Adjust proxy idle timeout to 120s in canary for region-us-east-1.

Alex (Support): I'll update the customer with the mitigation (client heartbeat) and the plan (server changes + new metric). Jordan — can you confirm after adding heartbeat whether partial outputs stop? If still occurring please upload a new pcap and the browser network HAR.

Jordan (Customer): Will do. ETA for client change: 2h. We will test and report back. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Sam (Eng): One more troubleshooting note: if you need to correlate pcap with logs, run this to get stream-id from TLS session: `openssl s_client -connect edge.redwood.ai:443 -showcerts` won't help; instead use `ngrep -W byline -q -d any 'GET /v1/streams' tcp` and correlate via `x-stream-id` header.

Mira (SRE): Marking follow-up tickets: SRE-1209 (billing-safe-stream-error), SRE-1210 (increase-proxy-timeout-canary), MET-4021 (billing_terminated_streams panel).

Alex (Support): Closing thread for now; will reopen if customer reproduces after heartbeat.

Jordan (Customer): Update (1906008585): heartbeat fix reduced idle-time disconnects; seeing one less mid-stream billing abort today after 3 hours of tests. Will report if it recurs.
